words.enDefinition: The study of decisions whose results depend on the choices of multiple participants.

examples.en: Our group used game theory to study how two clubs decided whether to share a room.
examples.zh: 我们组用「博弈论」研究两个社团如何决定是否共用一间教室。

examples.en: The tutor introduced game theory with an exercise about choosing times for a shared workshop.
examples.zh: 老师用一个选择共享工作坊时段的练习介绍了「博弈论」。

words.enDefinition: A choice a player is allowed to make at a particular point in a game.

examples.en: Choosing the larger room was an available action until another team booked it in the exercise.
examples.zh: 在另一队预订大教室之前，选大教室在练习中是一项「可选行动」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked which available action had the highest payoff after the other club chose Tuesday.
examples.zh: 老师问，另一个社团选了周二后，哪项「可选行动」的收益最高。

words.enDefinition: The collection of actions available to a player at a specified decision point.

examples.en: We listed the action set before discussing what each group could choose during the first round.
examples.zh: 我们先列出「行动集合」，再讨论各组第一轮能选什么。

examples.en: The tutor narrowed the action set to the rooms that were actually free that afternoon.
examples.zh: 老师把「行动集合」限定为当天下午实际空着的教室。

words.enDefinition: The collection of complete plans a player is allowed to use in a game.

examples.en: Our worksheet listed each player's strategy set before constructing the table of possible payoffs.
examples.zh: 练习表在构建可能收益表之前，列出了每位参与者的「策略集合」。

examples.en: The strategy set grew when we added another possible response to the shared booking game.
examples.zh: 我们给共同预订博弈增添一种可能应对之后，「策略集合」变大了。

words.enDefinition: A deterministic plan assigning an action at every possible information set of the player.

examples.en: The exercise asked us to write a pure strategy with a definite response to every possible offer.
examples.zh: 练习要求我们写出一种「纯策略」，为每个可能的提议确定明确的回应。

examples.en: Our first pure strategy always selected the early slot, regardless of the other team's choice.
examples.zh: 我们的第一种「纯策略」总是选择较早的时段，无论另一队怎么选。

collocations: specify a pure strategy on a game tree

words.enDefinition: A probability distribution over a player's pure strategies.

examples.en: We described a mixed strategy that assigned equal probabilities to the two complete plans on the worksheet.
examples.zh: 我们描述了一种「混合策略」，为练习表上的两个完整方案分配相等的概率。

examples.en: The tutor compared the expected payoffs from each mixed strategy in the classroom game.
examples.zh: 老师比较了课堂博弈中各种「混合策略」的期望收益。

collocations: choose probabilities for a mixed strategy

words.enDefinition: A plan specifying probabilities over available actions separately at each information set of an extensive-form game.

examples.en: The worksheet described a behavioral strategy by assigning probabilities to the available moves at each information set.
examples.zh: 练习表给各信息集下可选的行动分配概率，以描述一种「行为策略」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how the behavioral strategy changed at the later stage of the booking game.
examples.zh: 老师问，「行为策略」在预订博弈的后期阶段是怎样变化的。

collocations: compare a behavioral strategy with mixing over plans

words.enDefinition: A plan whose prescribed action depends on what the player observes or on which situation arises.

examples.en: The group chose a contingent strategy that used the smaller room if the larger one was booked.
examples.zh: 小组采用「条件式策略」，如果大教室被预订，就改用小教室。

examples.en: We read the contingent strategy to see what the second club would do after each possible offer.
examples.zh: 我们查看「条件式策略」，了解面对每种可能的提议，第二个社团会怎样做。

collocations: write a contingent strategy for later choices

words.enDefinition: A specification of one strategy for every player in a game.

examples.en: The model evaluated a strategy profile after both groups had chosen plans for every possible situation.
examples.zh: 两个小组都为各种可能情况选好应对计划后，模型评估了一个「策略组合」。

examples.en: We changed one plan within the strategy profile and left the other group's plan unchanged.
examples.zh: 我们改变了「策略组合」中的一个计划，另一组的计划仍保持原样。

collocations: check whether a strategy profile is an equilibrium

words.enDefinition: A list specifying one action for each player in a game.

examples.en: The action profile recorded which workshop session each of the two clubs actually chose.
examples.zh: 「行动组合」记录了两个社团各自实际选择的工作坊时段。

examples.en: We compared the payoffs for each action profile before looking for a stable pair of choices.
examples.zh: 寻找一对稳定的选择前，我们比较了各个「行动组合」的收益。

collocations: compute payoffs for an action profile

words.enDefinition: A rule assigning a numerical payoff to a player for each outcome or combination of strategies.

examples.en: The payoff function gave each team extra points when both booked the same workshop session.
examples.zh: 两队预订同一场工作坊时，「收益函数」给每队额外积分。

examples.en: The tutor changed the payoff function to include the inconvenience of using the smaller room.
examples.zh: 老师修改「收益函数」，计入使用小教室所带来的不便。

words.enDefinition: The ordered list of numerical payoffs received by all players at a particular outcome.

examples.en: The payoff vector listed the first team's points before the points awarded to the second team.
examples.zh: 「收益向量」先列第一队的积分，再列第二队获得的积分。

examples.en: We compared each payoff vector to see whether both groups gained from sharing the studio.
examples.zh: 我们对比各个「收益向量」，查看共用工作室能否让两组都受益。

words.enDefinition: A table of payoffs for the combinations of strategies in a strategic-form game.

examples.en: The payoff matrix showed the points both groups received for each pair of arrival times.
examples.zh: 「收益矩阵」显示每对到达时刻下两个小组各自所得的积分。

examples.en: Our tutor drew a payoff matrix to compare choices made without seeing the other group's decision.
examples.zh: 老师画了一个「收益矩阵」，比较双方都看不到对方决定时作出的选择。

collocations: fill in the cells of a payoff matrix

words.enDefinition: The probability-weighted average payoff from the possible outcomes of a choice or strategy.

examples.en: We calculated the expected payoff for each plan using the probabilities listed in the exercise.
examples.zh: 我们用练习中列出的概率计算每个方案的「期望收益」。

examples.en: The tutor asked which plan had a higher expected payoff against the other team's random choice.
examples.zh: 老师问，面对另一队随机选择时，哪个方案的「期望收益」更高。

words.enDefinition: The ordering of a player's possible results from higher to lower payoff or the reverse.

examples.en: The payoff ranking changed after the worksheet increased the value of using the larger room.
examples.zh: 练习表提高使用大教室的价值后，「收益排序」发生了变化。

examples.en: We checked whether both clubs had the same payoff ranking for the three booking outcomes.
examples.zh: 我们核对了两个社团对三种预订结果的「收益排序」是否相同。

words.enDefinition: A game represented by its players, strategies and payoffs for each strategy profile.

examples.en: We represented the booking exercise as a strategic-form game with two strategies for each club.
examples.zh: 我们把预订练习表示为「战略式博弈」，每个社团有两种策略。

examples.en: The tutor asked which information a strategic-form game retained when we stopped drawing the move sequence.
examples.zh: 老师问，不再绘制行动顺序后，「战略式博弈」保留了什么信息。

collocations: write a strategic-form game as a table

words.enDefinition: A game representation specifying move order, available actions, information, chance events and final payoffs.

examples.en: The extensive-form game showed who chose first and what the second team could observe.
examples.zh: 「扩展式博弈」展示谁先选，以及第二队能观察到什么。

examples.en: We converted the proposed room exchange into an extensive-form game before analysing the later choices.
examples.zh: 我们先把拟议的教室互换表示为「扩展式博弈」，再分析后续选择。

collocations: represent an extensive-form game as a tree

words.enDefinition: A game in which players make the relevant choices without observing one another's current moves beforehand.

examples.en: The simultaneous-move game required each team to submit its preferred time without seeing the other submission.
examples.zh: 「同时行动博弈」要求各队在看不到对方提交内容时提交自己偏好的时段。

examples.en: Our tutor compared a simultaneous-move game with a version where the second club could observe the first.
examples.zh: 老师把「同时行动博弈」与第二个社团能观察第一个社团选择的版本作了比较。

words.enDefinition: A game where players make their decisions in an ordered sequence.

examples.en: The booking model became a sequential-move game once the clubs were assigned different decision times.
examples.zh: 给各社团安排不同的决策时间后，预订模型变为「序贯行动博弈」。

examples.en: We traced the moves in the sequential-move game before deciding which plans the players would use.
examples.zh: 判断各参与者将采用哪些计划之前，我们先追踪了「序贯行动博弈」中的行动。

words.enDefinition: A game with finitely many players and finitely many pure strategies for each player.

examples.en: We treated the classroom exercise as a finite game because each club had only three possible plans.
examples.zh: 我们将课堂练习视为「有限博弈」，因为每个社团只有三个可能计划。

examples.en: Our tutor enumerated the possible outcomes of the finite game before examining each player's best choice.
examples.zh: 老师先列出了「有限博弈」的各种可能结果，再考察每位参与者的最佳选择。

collocations: analyse a finite game in strategic form

words.enDefinition: A game in which the players' payoffs add up to zero at every outcome.

examples.en: In the zero-sum game, any points gained by one team were lost by the other.
examples.zh: 在「零和博弈」中，一队获得多少积分，另一队就失去多少。

examples.en: The tutor asked which feature made the example a zero-sum game regardless of the chosen actions.
examples.zh: 老师问，什么特征使例题无论选择何种行动都属于「零和博弈」。

words.enDefinition: A game in which the sum of players' payoffs is the same at every outcome.

examples.en: The constant-sum game allocated exactly ten tokens between the two groups for every possible outcome.
examples.zh: 「常和博弈」的每种结果都在两组之间分配恰好十枚代币。

examples.en: We checked each outcome to confirm that the classroom example really was a constant-sum game.
examples.zh: 我们逐一核对结果，确认课堂示例确实是「常和博弈」。

collocations: compare outcomes in a constant-sum game

words.enDefinition: A game in which the total payoff differs across at least two possible outcomes.

examples.en: The exercise became a variable-sum game because both groups gained points when their choices matched.
examples.zh: 两组选择一致时，两组都能得分，因此练习成为「变和博弈」。

examples.en: Our tutor compared a variable-sum game with a contest where the same number of tokens was always distributed.
examples.zh: 老师把「变和博弈」与每次都分配同样数量代币的竞赛作了比较。

collocations: distinguish a variable-sum game from a constant-sum one

words.enDefinition: Information everyone knows, everyone knows that everyone knows, and so on through every level.

examples.en: The exercise assumed the rules were common knowledge before either club selected a time.
examples.zh: 练习假定规则是「共同知识」，然后两个社团才选择时段。

examples.en: We discussed why posting the scoring rule publicly could help make it common knowledge among the teams.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了为什么公开张贴计分规则有助于让规则成为各队间的「共同知识」。

words.enDefinition: a setting where the structure and payoff functions of the game are known to all players

examples.en: Our worksheet assumed complete information, so each participant knew how both teams valued the two rooms.
examples.zh: 练习表假定「完全信息」，因此各参与者都知道两队怎样评价两间教室。

examples.en: The tutor distinguished complete information about payoffs from actually seeing what the other team had chosen.
examples.zh: 老师区分了关于收益的「完全信息」和实际看到另一队作出的选择。

collocations: model a game with complete information
compare complete information with private types

words.enDefinition: A game where some payoff-relevant information, such as a player's type or valuation, is privately known.

examples.en: The exercise used a game of incomplete information because each club knew only its own room valuation.
examples.zh: 练习用「不完全信息博弈」，因为各社团只知道自己对教室的估值。

examples.en: Our tutor asked which details were private in the game of incomplete information on the worksheet.
examples.zh: 老师问，练习表里的「不完全信息博弈」中哪些细节是私有的。

collocations: model a game of incomplete information
solve a game of incomplete information
specify types in a game of incomplete information

words.enDefinition: A game in which each player observes the complete previous history whenever they make a decision.

examples.en: The perfect-information game let each group see all earlier choices before making its next move.
examples.zh: 「完美信息博弈」让各组在作出下一次行动前看见所有先前选择。

examples.en: Our tutor showed where the second club moved in the perfect-information game about allocating rooms.
examples.zh: 老师展示了在分配教室的「完美信息博弈」中，第二个社团在哪一步行动。

collocations: use backward induction in a perfect-information game

words.enDefinition: A game in which at least one player cannot observe the full history at a decision point.

examples.en: The classroom exercise became an imperfect-information game when the second team could not see the first choice.
examples.zh: 第二队看不到第一队的选择后，课堂练习变成了「不完美信息博弈」。

examples.en: We labelled the indistinguishable situations before analysing the imperfect-information game on the board.
examples.zh: 分析黑板上的「不完美信息博弈」之前，我们标出了无法区分的几种情形。

collocations: specify information sets in an imperfect-information game

words.enDefinition: A collection of decision points a player cannot distinguish when choosing an action.

examples.en: The tutor joined the two decision points to indicate a single information set for that player.
examples.zh: 老师把两个决策点连起来，表示对该参与者而言它们属于同一个「信息集」。

examples.en: Our diagram used an information set because the second club did not know which move had occurred.
examples.zh: 因为第二个社团不知道先前发生了哪项行动，我们在图中用了一个「信息集」。

collocations: assign beliefs to an information set

words.enDefinition: A branching representation of a game's move sequence, decision situations and possible endings.

examples.en: We drew a game tree to show how different offers led to different responses.
examples.zh: 我们画了一棵「博弈树」，展示不同提议怎样引出不同回应。

examples.en: The tutor added another branch to the game tree when the second club could suggest Tuesday.
examples.zh: 第二个社团可以提议周二时，老师在「博弈树」上又加了一个分支。

collocations: trace a path through a game tree
label payoffs on a game tree

words.enDefinition: The sequence of actions and chance events that has occurred along part of a game.

examples.en: The game history recorded which rooms had been proposed and whether each offer was accepted.
examples.zh: 「博弈历史」记录了各方提议过哪些教室，以及每个提议是否被接受。

examples.en: We changed our plan after reading the game history from the earlier rounds of the exercise.
examples.zh: 读过练习前几轮的「博弈历史」后，我们改变了计划。

collocations: condition a move on the game history

words.enDefinition: A complete sequence of moves and chance events ending at a final outcome of the game.

examples.en: The terminal history ended with both groups accepting the proposed workshop times on the board.
examples.zh: 「终局历史」以两组都接受黑板所列工作坊时段结束。

examples.en: We recorded the full sequence of choices before assigning payoffs to the terminal history.
examples.zh: 我们先记录完整的选择顺序，再给「终局历史」赋予收益。

collocations: assign payoffs to a terminal history
compare the payoffs at different terminal histories

words.enDefinition: The root of a game tree, representing the situation before any move has been made.

examples.en: We marked the initial node before drawing the first two options in the classroom game.
examples.zh: 我们先标出「博弈起始节点」，再把课堂博弈最初的两个选项画出来。

examples.en: The worksheet attached two arrows to the initial node to represent the first club's choices.
examples.zh: 练习表从「博弈起始节点」引出两条箭头，表示第一个社团的选择。

collocations: draw branches from the initial node

words.enDefinition: A move another player can see or verify before making a relevant decision.

examples.en: The second club could respond because the room booking was an observable move in the model.
examples.zh: 因为模型中的教室预订是「可观察行动」，第二个社团可以作出回应。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether the initial offer counted as an observable move for all participants.
examples.zh: 老师问，对所有参与者而言，最初的提议是否属于「可观察行动」。

collocations: distinguish an observable move from a hidden one
condition a choice on an observable move

words.enDefinition: A strategy giving the highest payoff against a specified strategy choice by the other players.

examples.en: The worksheet marked Tuesday as a best response when the other club had already selected Tuesday.
examples.zh: 另一社团已经选了周二时，练习表把周二标为一个「最佳反应」。

examples.en: We calculated a best response after fixing the other team's choices in the classroom exercise.
examples.zh: 在课堂练习中，我们固定另一队的选择以后，计算了一个「最佳反应」。

collocations: mark a best response in the matrix

words.enDefinition: A mapping assigning the set of all payoff-maximizing strategies to each possible choice by other players.

examples.en: The best-response correspondence included both room choices when the two generated exactly the same payoff.
examples.zh: 两间教室带来的收益完全相同时，「最佳反应对应」包含了两种选择。

examples.en: We used the best-response correspondence to check whether more than one plan was optimal.
examples.zh: 我们用「最佳反应对应」核查是否有不止一个最优方案。

words.enDefinition: A single-valued rule giving a player's payoff-maximizing choice for each choice of the other players.

examples.en: The exercise derived a best-response function because each scheduling choice had one optimal reply.
examples.zh: 练习推导出一个「最佳反应函数」，因为每种排期选择只有一种最优回应。

examples.en: We plotted the best-response function for one club before comparing it with the other club's function.
examples.zh: 我们先画出一个社团的「最佳反应函数」，再和另一社团的函数作比较。

collocations: find where two best-response functions intersect

words.enDefinition: A process in which players repeatedly revise their choices to best respond to others' current choices.

examples.en: The simulator showed best-response dynamics when each team reconsidered its room choice after observing the other.
examples.zh: 各队观察对方后重新考虑教室选择时，模拟器展示了「最佳反应动态」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether best-response dynamics would ever settle on one pair of choices in the exercise.
examples.zh: 老师问，练习中的「最佳反应动态」最后是否会稳定在一对选择上。

words.enDefinition: A strategy giving a higher payoff than each alternative for every strategy choice of the other players.

examples.en: Tuesday was a strictly dominant strategy because it gave the first club more points in every case.
examples.zh: 周二是「严格占优策略」，因为在每种情况下它都给第一个社团更多积分。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether either player had a strictly dominant strategy in the room-sharing exercise.
examples.zh: 老师问，在共用教室的练习里，有没有参与者存在「严格占优策略」。

collocations: check for a strictly dominant strategy

words.enDefinition: A strategy that does at least as well as each alternative in every case, with some strict advantage.

examples.en: The example showed a weakly dominant strategy because one choice tied in one column and won elsewhere.
examples.zh: 一种选择在一列中打平、其余列都更好，例题以此展示「弱占优策略」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked where the payoffs tied for the weakly dominant strategy in the small matrix.
examples.zh: 老师问，在这个小矩阵里，「弱占优策略」在哪些情形下的收益与另一策略持平。

collocations: check the ties for a weakly dominant strategy

words.enDefinition: A strategy that yields a lower payoff than a particular alternative against every choice of the other players.

examples.en: We crossed out a strictly dominated strategy after finding another plan with higher payoffs in every column.
examples.zh: 发现另一个方案在每一列的收益都更高后，我们划掉了一个「被严格支配的策略」。

examples.en: The tutor asked why a strictly dominated strategy was never a best response in the example.
examples.zh: 老师问，为什么例题中「被严格支配的策略」从来不是最佳反应。

collocations: compare a strictly dominated strategy with its alternative

words.enDefinition: A strategy that an alternative matches or beats in every case and strictly beats in at least one case.

examples.en: A weakly dominated strategy remained tied in one column but gave fewer points in another column.
examples.zh: 一个「被弱支配的策略」在一列里仍能打平，但在另一列得分更少。

examples.en: Our tutor checked both columns before calling the second option a weakly dominated strategy.
examples.zh: 老师核对了两列数值，才把第二个选项称为「被弱支配的策略」。

collocations: compare a weakly dominated strategy with an alternative

words.expression: iterated elimination of strictly dominated strategies
words.lemma: iterated elimination of strictly dominated strategies
words.zhGloss: 反复剔除被严格支配策略
words.enDefinition: Repeatedly removing strictly dominated strategies and reassessing remaining options in the reduced game.
acceptedZhAnswers: 反复剔除被严格支配策略
acceptedEnVariants: iterated elimination of strictly dominated strategies

examples.en: We used iterated elimination of strictly dominated strategies to simplify the classroom game one step at a time.
examples.zh: 我们用「反复剔除被严格支配策略」逐步简化课堂博弈。

examples.en: The tutor illustrated iterated elimination of strictly dominated strategies by crossing out rows, then checking the remaining columns.
examples.zh: 老师先划去若干行，再检查剩下的列，以说明「反复剔除被严格支配策略」。

collocations: apply iterated elimination of strictly dominated strategies
solve a game by iterated elimination of strictly dominated strategies
explain iterated elimination of strictly dominated strategies

words.zhGloss: 可通过支配关系求解的博弈
words.enDefinition: In the strict-dominance setting, a game with one strategy profile left after repeated elimination of dominated strategies.
acceptedZhAnswers: 可通过支配关系求解的博弈

examples.en: Our worksheet presented a dominance-solvable game with a single pair of choices remaining after the eliminations.
examples.zh: 练习表给出一个「可通过支配关系求解的博弈」，剔除之后只剩一对选择。

examples.en: The class checked whether the revised payoff matrix still described a dominance-solvable game.
examples.zh: 同学们检查了修改后的收益矩阵是否仍表示一种「可通过支配关系求解的博弈」。

words.enDefinition: A strategy that is a best response to a belief about other strategies consistent with common belief in rationality.

examples.en: The worksheet asked which belief about the other team's choice could support a rationalizable strategy.
examples.zh: 练习表问，关于另一队选择的哪一种信念能支持一个「可理性化策略」。

examples.en: Our tutor showed that a rationalizable strategy could remain even when it appeared in no Nash equilibrium.
examples.zh: 老师说明，一个「可理性化策略」即使没有出现在任何纳什均衡中，也可能保留下来。

collocations: test whether a strategy is a rationalizable strategy
a belief supporting a rationalizable strategy

words.enDefinition: A strategy profile in which no player can gain by changing strategy alone.

examples.en: The class found a Nash equilibrium where neither club benefited from changing its own booking choice.
examples.zh: 全班找到了一个「纳什均衡」，在该组合中两个社团都无法靠单独改变时段选择获益。

examples.en: We tested each possible Nash equilibrium by keeping one team's choice fixed while checking the other's options.
examples.zh: 我们固定一队的选择、检查另一队的选项，以检验每个可能的「纳什均衡」。

words.enDefinition: A Nash equilibrium in which each player uses a deterministic strategy.

examples.en: The exercise had a pure-strategy Nash equilibrium where both clubs chose the same afternoon session.
examples.zh: 练习存在一个「纯策略纳什均衡」，两个社团都选同一场下午活动。

examples.en: We checked each cell to see whether the classroom contest had a pure-strategy Nash equilibrium.
examples.zh: 我们逐格检查课堂竞赛是否存在「纯策略纳什均衡」。

collocations: show a pure-strategy Nash equilibrium in the matrix

words.enDefinition: A Nash equilibrium in which players use probability distributions over pure strategies and at least one genuinely randomizes.

examples.en: The tutor derived a mixed-strategy Nash equilibrium for a game with no stable pair of pure choices.
examples.zh: 老师为一个没有稳定纯策略组合的博弈推导了「混合策略纳什均衡」。

examples.en: We verified the mixed-strategy Nash equilibrium by checking that neither team gained from changing its probabilities.
examples.zh: 我们检查了两队都不能靠单独改变概率而获益，以验证「混合策略纳什均衡」。

collocations: calculate probabilities for a mixed-strategy Nash equilibrium

words.enDefinition: The payoff a player receives, or expects to receive, under an equilibrium strategy profile.

examples.en: We calculated each club's equilibrium payoff after finding the stable pair of room choices.
examples.zh: 找到稳定的教室选择组合之后，我们计算了各社团的「均衡收益」。

examples.en: The tutor compared the equilibrium payoff with what the same group earned when both teams cooperated.
examples.zh: 老师把「均衡收益」与两队都合作时同一小组的所得作了比较。

words.enDefinition: A change in one player's strategy while all other players keep their strategies fixed.

examples.en: The worksheet tested a unilateral deviation by switching one club's session while leaving the other unchanged.
examples.zh: 练习表检验一个「单边偏离」，即改变一个社团的时段，另一个保持不变。

examples.en: We considered each unilateral deviation before confirming that the proposed choices formed an equilibrium.
examples.zh: 我们考察了每种「单边偏离」，再确认所提议的选择组合是否构成均衡。

collocations: rule out gains from a unilateral deviation

words.enDefinition: A change in a player's strategy that improves its own payoff when the others do not change theirs.

examples.en: The first team found a profitable deviation because switching rooms gave it more points in that row.
examples.zh: 第一队找到了一个「有利偏离」，因为在该行换教室能让它获得更多积分。

examples.en: Our tutor checked for a profitable deviation before calling the pair of choices an equilibrium.
examples.zh: 老师先查看是否存在「有利偏离」，再把这对选择称为均衡。

collocations: identify a profitable deviation from an outcome

words.enDefinition: equality of a player's expected payoffs for options assigned positive probability in a mixed equilibrium

examples.en: The tutor wrote an indifference condition to make both options in the mixture equally attractive.
examples.zh: 老师写下一个「无差异条件」，使混合策略里的两个选项同样有吸引力。

examples.en: We used the indifference condition before checking whether a third option would give a higher payoff.
examples.zh: 在检查第三个选项能否给出更高收益之前，我们先用了「无差异条件」。

collocations: check the indifference condition for two strategies

words.enDefinition: The set of pure strategies assigned strictly positive probability by a mixed strategy.

examples.en: The support of a mixed strategy included both times but excluded the room that was never selected.
examples.zh: 「混合策略的支撑集」包括两个时段，但不包括从未被选中的教室选项。

examples.en: Our tutor listed the support of a mixed strategy after calculating the probabilities in the example.
examples.zh: 老师算出例题中的概率后，列出了「混合策略的支撑集」。

collocations: identify the support of a mixed strategy
find strategies outside the support of a mixed strategy
check the support of a mixed strategy

words.enDefinition: A mixed strategy assigning strictly positive probability to every available pure strategy of that player.

examples.en: The example used a completely mixed strategy with positive probability on each of the three alternatives.
examples.zh: 例题使用「完全混合策略」，三个备选方案的概率都为正。

examples.en: We checked whether the distribution was a completely mixed strategy after assigning zero probability to Tuesday.
examples.zh: 将周二的概率设为零后，我们检查该分布是否仍属「完全混合策略」。

collocations: draw probabilities for a completely mixed strategy

words.enDefinition: Choosing or predicting one equilibrium when the same game allows several.

examples.en: The class discussed equilibrium selection because either shared booking time could be stable in the model.
examples.zh: 模型中的两个共同预订时段都可能是稳定的，全班因此讨论了「均衡选择」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether a prominent time on the timetable might influence equilibrium selection.
examples.zh: 老师问，日程表上显眼的时段是否会影响「均衡选择」。

words.enDefinition: Two or more distinct equilibrium strategy profiles in the same game.

examples.en: The scheduling example had multiple equilibria because the clubs could coordinate on either of two days.
examples.zh: 排期例题存在「多个均衡」，因为两个社团在两天中的哪一天都可以协调一致。

examples.en: We checked the payoff matrix for multiple equilibria after changing the points awarded for sharing equipment.
examples.zh: 我们改变共用设备获得的积分之后，核查收益矩阵里是否有「多个均衡」。

words.enDefinition: A salient choice that can help players coordinate without direct agreement.

examples.en: The main entrance served as a Schelling point in the classroom example about meeting without messages.
examples.zh: 在不发消息碰面的课堂例题里，正门充当了「谢林焦点」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked why the clock tower might become a Schelling point for both groups.
examples.zh: 老师问，钟楼为什么可能成为两个小组的「谢林焦点」。

collocations: discuss how a Schelling point emerges

words.enDefinition: an equilibrium weakly preferred by every player to the other equilibria, with at least one player strictly preferring it to each alternative considered

examples.en: The example's payoff-dominant equilibrium gave both clubs more points than coordinating on the smaller room.
examples.zh: 例题中的「收益占优均衡」比双方协调使用小教室时给两个社团更多积分。

examples.en: We checked the payoffs of both teams before labelling one outcome a payoff-dominant equilibrium.
examples.zh: 在把一个结果称为「收益占优均衡」之前，我们核查了两个小组的收益。

collocations: compare a payoff-dominant equilibrium with another outcome
a payoff-dominant equilibrium in a coordination game

words.enDefinition: In a symmetric two-action coordination game, the equilibrium with a strategy that pays more against equal mixing.

examples.en: Both choosing the smaller room formed the risk-dominant equilibrium because that choice paid more against equal mixing.
examples.zh: 双方都选小教室构成「风险占优均衡」，因为当对方以相同概率选择两个选项时，选小教室的期望收益更高。

examples.en: Our tutor checked the risk-dominant equilibrium by assuming the other club was equally likely to choose either option.
examples.zh: 老师假定另一社团选择两个选项的概率各半，据此核查「风险占优均衡」。

collocations: compare a risk-dominant equilibrium with a payoff-dominant one
explain a risk-dominant equilibrium with a matrix

words.enDefinition: A game in which players gain by aligning their choices in one of the compatible ways.

examples.en: The coordination game rewarded both groups when they independently picked the same slot for the workshop.
examples.zh: 两组各自为工作坊选择同一时段时，「协调博弈」会让双方都获得奖励。

examples.en: Our tutor used a coordination game to discuss how conventions could develop between neighbouring clubs.
examples.zh: 老师用「协调博弈」讨论邻近社团之间怎样形成惯例。

collocations: identify equilibria in a coordination game

words.enDefinition: A game in which players benefit when their choices differ in suitable ways.

examples.en: The anti-coordination game gave both teams more points for choosing different equipment stations at the same time.
examples.zh: 两队同时选择不同设备工位时，「反协调博弈」给双方更多积分。

examples.en: We used an anti-coordination game to model dividing two jobs when either team could perform them.
examples.zh: 两项工作任一队都能完成，我们用「反协调博弈」给分工建模。

collocations: find equilibria in an anti-coordination game

words.enDefinition: A coordination game where mutual cooperation pays most, while a safer action protects against unmatched cooperation.

examples.en: The assurance game rewarded a joint project most, but either group could choose a smaller individual project.
examples.zh: 「保证博弈」给合作项目最高回报，但两组也都能选择较小的单独项目。

examples.en: Our tutor asked why uncertainty about the other group mattered so much in the assurance game.
examples.zh: 老师问，在「保证博弈」中，对另一组选择的不确定性为何如此重要。

collocations: compare equilibria in an assurance game

words.enDefinition: A two-player game where one player benefits when choices match and the other benefits when they differ.

examples.en: We played matching pennies with two marked cards and kept score using classroom points.
examples.zh: 我们用两张有标记的卡片玩「硬币匹配博弈」，用课堂积分记分。

examples.en: The tutor used matching pennies to show why no pair of fixed actions was stable.
examples.zh: 老师用「硬币匹配博弈」说明为什么不存在稳定的固定行动组合。

collocations: use matching pennies to illustrate mixed strategies

words.enDefinition: a game in which defection is individually dominant for each player while mutual cooperation gives both a better outcome

examples.en: The tutor illustrated a prisoner's dilemma with two clubs deciding whether to contribute to a shared project.
examples.zh: 老师用两个社团决定是否为共同项目出资来说明「囚徒困境」。

examples.en: The worksheet asked why both groups ended up with fewer points in the prisoner's dilemma example.
examples.zh: 练习表问，为什么「囚徒困境」例题中的两个小组最终都拿到较少积分。

collocations: identify the incentives in a prisoner's dilemma
play a repeated version of the prisoner's dilemma

words.enDefinition: An outcome in which both players choose the cooperative action.

examples.en: Mutual cooperation gave both clubs extra workshop time in the first case on the worksheet.
examples.zh: 练习表的第一个案例中，「双方合作」让两个社团都得到更多工作坊时间。

examples.en: We compared mutual cooperation with the outcome where only one team helped maintain the shared space.
examples.zh: 我们将「双方合作」与只有一队协助维护共享空间的结果作比较。

collocations: compare mutual cooperation with mutual defection
reach mutual cooperation in a repeated game

words.enDefinition: An outcome in which both players choose the noncooperative action.

examples.en: Mutual defection left the shared project without any tokens from either team in the exercise.
examples.zh: 在练习里，「双方背叛」意味着共享项目没有得到任一队的代币。

examples.en: Our tutor asked why mutual defection could be stable even though cooperation helped both clubs.
examples.zh: 老师问，虽然合作对两个社团都有利，「双方背叛」为什么可能保持稳定。

collocations: compare the payoffs under mutual defection

words.enDefinition: Solving a sequential game by finding optimal decisions at later stages and working back toward the start.

examples.en: We used backward induction to choose the last response before analysing which opening offer made sense.
examples.zh: 我们用「逆向归纳」先选最后一步的回应，再分析哪项初始提议合理。

examples.en: The tutor showed backward induction by moving from the leaves of the game tree to its root.
examples.zh: 老师从博弈树的叶节点回到根节点，演示了「逆向归纳」。

collocations: solve a game by backward induction
use backward induction on a tree

words.enDefinition: A game starting at a singleton information set, containing all successors without cutting through any information set.

examples.en: We checked whether the subgame included every possible response after the first club made its selection.
examples.zh: 第一个社团选定后，我们检查了「子博弈」是否涵盖随后的每种可能回应。

examples.en: The tutor asked why cutting the linked decision points would prevent that branch from being a subgame.
examples.zh: 老师问，为什么切开相连的决策点会使该分支无法构成「子博弈」。

collocations: check whether a branch begins a subgame

words.enDefinition: A subgame starting after the beginning of the original game and therefore excluding some of it.

examples.en: The diagram marked a proper subgame beginning after the second group received the opening proposal.
examples.zh: 图中标出一个「真子博弈」，它从第二组收到初始提议之后开始。

examples.en: We checked the proper subgame separately before studying the strategy profile from the original starting point.
examples.zh: 我们先单独检查「真子博弈」，再研究从原起点出发的策略组合。

collocations: count proper subgames in the tree

words.enDefinition: A strategy profile that forms a Nash equilibrium in every subgame, including the whole game.

examples.en: We tested a subgame-perfect equilibrium by checking the proposed plans after both possible first moves.
examples.zh: 我们检查了两种可能开局之后的拟议计划，以检验「子博弈完美均衡」。

examples.en: The tutor rejected one candidate for a subgame-perfect equilibrium because its later response was not optimal.
examples.zh: 老师否决了一个「子博弈完美均衡」候选方案，因为它在后期的回应不是最优。

collocations: derive a subgame-perfect equilibrium by backward induction

words.enDefinition: The part of a strategy governing choices after a specified history or stage.

examples.en: The worksheet asked us to state the continuation strategy after the second group declined the first proposal.
examples.zh: 练习表要求我们写出第二组拒绝首个提议之后的「后续策略」。

examples.en: Our tutor changed the continuation strategy while holding the opening choice fixed in the exercise.
examples.zh: 老师改变了练习中的「后续策略」，同时保持初始选择不变。

collocations: compare continuation strategies after different histories
check the continuation strategy at a later decision

words.enDefinition: The payoff expected from the remaining part of a game after a specified point or history.

examples.en: We calculated the continuation payoff from the remaining rounds before comparing the two actions available now.
examples.zh: 我们先算出余下各轮的「后续收益」，再比较当前可选的两项行动。

examples.en: The tutor asked how rejecting the offer would affect the group's continuation payoff in the example.
examples.zh: 老师问，拒绝该提议将怎样影响例题中小组的「后续收益」。

collocations: include the continuation payoff in an earlier decision

words.enDefinition: A sequence of moves that occurs under the specified equilibrium strategies, including possible chance outcomes.

examples.en: On the equilibrium path, the second club accepted the proposed time in the first round.
examples.zh: 沿「均衡路径」，第二个社团会在第一轮接受提议的时段。

examples.en: We traced an equilibrium path through the tree after identifying which strategy each player would use.
examples.zh: 确定各参与者采用的策略后，我们沿博弈树追踪了一条「均衡路径」。

words.enDefinition: A possible sequence of moves given zero probability by the equilibrium strategies.

examples.en: The tutor checked an off-equilibrium path to see how the second club would respond to an unexpected offer.
examples.zh: 老师核查了一条「均衡外路径」，看第二个社团会怎样回应意料之外的提议。

examples.en: We labelled the off-equilibrium path that began with an action excluded by the proposed strategies.
examples.zh: 我们标出了一条「均衡外路径」，它起于拟议策略不会选择的行动。

collocations: analyse choices on an off-equilibrium path
specify beliefs after an off-equilibrium path

words.enDefinition: Optimality of a player's plan from each information set onward, given its beliefs and the other players' strategies.

examples.en: Our tutor checked sequential rationality even at decisions the proposed strategies would never reach.
examples.zh: 即使某些决策点按拟议策略永远不会到达，老师也核查了「序贯理性」。

examples.en: The worksheet asked whether the later response satisfied sequential rationality under the beliefs shown.
examples.zh: 练习表问，在所示信念下，后期回应是否满足「序贯理性」。

collocations: check sequential rationality at each information set

words.enDefinition: A specification of the probabilities players assign to possible nodes at their information sets.

examples.en: We wrote a belief system showing how likely the second club thought each earlier choice was.
examples.zh: 我们写出一套「信念体系」，说明第二个社团认为先前各选择的可能性有多大。

examples.en: The tutor changed the belief system to see whether the preferred response would also change.
examples.zh: 老师改变了「信念体系」，查看最受青睐的回应是否也会变化。

collocations: check a belief system for consistency

words.enDefinition: Revising beliefs using Bayes' rule after observing new evidence.

examples.en: The worksheet used Bayesian updating to revise the group's beliefs after it observed the first offer.
examples.zh: 小组看到初始提议后，练习表用「贝叶斯更新」修正其信念。

examples.en: We checked whether Bayesian updating was possible when the observed action had zero probability in equilibrium.
examples.zh: 观测行动在均衡下概率为零时，我们核查了能否直接进行「贝叶斯更新」。

collocations: compare beliefs before and after Bayesian updating

words.enDefinition: A model representing incomplete information with player types, beliefs and strategies contingent on types.

examples.en: The bidding worksheet used a Bayesian game in which each participant knew only their own valuation.
examples.zh: 竞价练习表用了一个「贝叶斯博弈」，各参与者只知道自己的估值。

examples.en: Our tutor introduced a Bayesian game by asking what the clubs knew about each other's priorities.
examples.zh: 老师通过询问各社团对对方优先事项了解多少，介绍了「贝叶斯博弈」。

collocations: specify the types in a Bayesian game

words.enDefinition: A player's private information or characteristics that matter for payoffs or beliefs in a game.

examples.en: The example assigned a player type according to how much each club valued the larger room.
examples.zh: 例题根据各社团对大教室的重视程度给它们分配「参与者类型」。

examples.en: We listed the available responses for each player type before analysing the classroom auction.
examples.zh: 分析课堂拍卖之前，我们列出了各「参与者类型」可选的回应。

collocations: infer a player type from observed choices
condition a strategy on player type

words.enDefinition: A probability distribution over the possible private types of players in a game.

examples.en: The workshop model used a type distribution to represent uncertainty about each group's valuation.
examples.zh: 工作坊模型用「类型概率分布」表示对各组估值的不确定性。

examples.en: We changed the type distribution before recalculating the expected payoffs for the two possible plans.
examples.zh: 我们先改变「类型概率分布」，再重新计算两个可能方案的预期收益。

collocations: draw values from a type distribution
compare outcomes under different type distributions

words.enDefinition: A strategy profile where each type maximizes expected payoff given its information and the other players' strategies.

examples.en: Our tutor derived a Bayesian Nash equilibrium in the example where both bidders had private valuations.
examples.zh: 老师在两位竞价者都有私有估值的例题中推导出一个「贝叶斯纳什均衡」。

examples.en: We checked whether each type wanted to change its plan before confirming the Bayesian Nash equilibrium.
examples.zh: 我们先检查各类参与者是否想改变计划，再确认「贝叶斯纳什均衡」。

collocations: compute expected payoffs in a Bayesian Nash equilibrium

words.enDefinition: Strategies and beliefs such that decisions are sequentially rational and beliefs follow Bayes' rule where applicable.

examples.en: The worksheet listed both strategies and beliefs before testing a perfect Bayesian equilibrium in the sequential example.
examples.zh: 练习表先列出策略和信念，再检验序贯例题中的「完美贝叶斯均衡」。

examples.en: Our tutor checked the response to an unexpected offer when evaluating the proposed perfect Bayesian equilibrium.
examples.zh: 老师在评估拟议的「完美贝叶斯均衡」时，核查了对意外提议的回应。

collocations: specify beliefs in a perfect Bayesian equilibrium

words.enDefinition: a sequentially rational assessment consistent with a limit of completely mixed strategy profiles and the corresponding Bayesian beliefs

examples.en: Our tutor illustrated sequential equilibrium by considering small positive probabilities for all available moves.
examples.zh: 老师通过给所有可选行动考虑很小的正概率来说明「序贯均衡」。

examples.en: The worksheet checked which beliefs could arise in the limit before confirming the sequential equilibrium.
examples.zh: 练习表先核查哪些信念能在取极限时出现，再确认「序贯均衡」。

collocations: test beliefs for consistency in a sequential equilibrium

words.enDefinition: A commitment others have reason to believe because later choices are constrained or following through remains worthwhile.

examples.en: The example treated the fixed room booking as a credible commitment because it could not be changed.
examples.zh: 由于教室预订一经确定便无法更改，例题把它视为「可信承诺」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked why the other group would take a credible commitment into account before choosing.
examples.zh: 老师问，另一组为什么会在作选择前考虑「可信承诺」。

words.enDefinition: a promised future action that the promiser has incentives to carry out when choosing whether to do it

examples.en: The worksheet asked whether sharing spare materials later was a credible promise for the first team.
examples.zh: 练习表问，对第一队来说，之后分享备用材料是否构成「可信许诺」。

examples.en: We examined the later incentives before deciding whether the group had made a credible promise.
examples.zh: 我们先考察后期激励，再判断该组是否作出了「可信许诺」。

collocations: distinguish a credible promise from an empty one

words.enDefinition: An arrangement that makes a planned future choice more credible by limiting or changing later options.

examples.en: A locked form served as a commitment device because teams could not revise submitted times.
examples.zh: 锁定的表单成了「承诺装置」，因为各队不能修改已经提交的时段。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how removing the commitment device changed the options available in the next round.
examples.zh: 老师问，取消「承诺装置」会怎样改变下一轮的可选项。

collocations: design a commitment device for a model

words.enDefinition: A benefit from acting later, such as being able to respond to the first player's observable choice.

examples.en: The second-mover advantage came from seeing the first group's preference before suggesting another workshop time.
examples.zh: 「后行动者优势」来自先看到第一组的偏好，再提议另一个工作坊时段。

examples.en: The tutor asked whether the second-mover advantage disappeared when the earlier choice was hidden.
examples.zh: 老师问，先前的选择被隐藏时，「后行动者优势」是否消失。

collocations: compare outcomes with a second-mover advantage

words.enDefinition: A game formed by playing the same underlying stage game on multiple occasions.

examples.en: The class used a repeated game to see whether two teams would keep sharing equipment over time.
examples.zh: 全班用「重复博弈」查看两队是否会一直共用设备。

examples.en: We compared the decisions in a repeated game with the ones made in a single round.
examples.zh: 我们把「重复博弈」中的决定与只进行一轮时的决定作了比较。

collocations: compare a repeated game with a single round

words.enDefinition: The underlying one-period game whose choices and payoffs recur in a repeated game.

examples.en: The stage game gave each team two ways to contribute to maintaining the shared study space.
examples.zh: 「阶段博弈」给各队两种为维护共享自习空间作贡献的方式。

examples.en: Our tutor drew the stage game before discussing what changed when the same interaction was repeated.
examples.zh: 老师先画出「阶段博弈」，再讨论同样互动重复进行时会发生什么变化。

words.enDefinition: A game repeating its stage game a known finite number of times.

examples.en: We played a finitely repeated game that ended after the fifth round of the classroom exercise.
examples.zh: 我们玩了一个「有限重复博弈」，到课堂练习第五轮结束就停止。

examples.en: Our worksheet asked what the groups would choose in the last round of the finitely repeated game.
examples.zh: 练习表问，各组在「有限重复博弈」的最后一轮会怎样选择。

collocations: identify the last round of a finitely repeated game

words.enDefinition: A model in which the same stage game is played over an unbounded sequence of periods.

examples.en: The worksheet introduced an infinitely repeated game without naming a final round for the shared project.
examples.zh: 练习表引入了「无限重复博弈」，没有给共同项目指定最后一轮。

examples.en: Our tutor discussed how valuing future meetings affected cooperation in the infinitely repeated game.
examples.zh: 老师讨论了对未来见面的重视程度怎样影响「无限重复博弈」中的合作。

collocations: model cooperation in an infinitely repeated game
calculate payoffs in an infinitely repeated game

words.enDefinition: A strategy whose prescribed actions can vary with previous observed events in a game.

examples.en: The class examined a history-dependent strategy that changed after one club stopped contributing to the activity.
examples.zh: 同学们考察了一种「依赖历史的策略」，一个社团不再为活动出资后，该策略随之变化。

examples.en: We wrote a history-dependent strategy for the shared equipment game before playing three practice rounds.
examples.zh: 我们先给共享设备博弈写出一种「依赖历史的策略」，再玩三轮练习。

collocations: use a history-dependent strategy in a repeated game

words.enDefinition: A strategy that changes a player's future behaviour when a specific event occurs in the game.

examples.en: The model used a trigger strategy that changed the next response after a missed contribution.
examples.zh: 模型采用一种「触发策略」，某次出资未发生后，下一步回应就会改变。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how long the response in the trigger strategy would last in the example.
examples.zh: 老师问，例题里「触发策略」中的回应会持续多久。

collocations: use a trigger strategy in a repeated game

words.enDefinition: A strategy that cooperates until a defection occurs and then permanently switches to the noncooperative action.

examples.en: The grim trigger strategy ended all future contributions after the other team first stopped contributing.
examples.zh: 另一队首次停止出资后，「严厉触发策略」会终止此后的所有出资。

examples.en: Our tutor compared a grim trigger strategy with a response lasting only one classroom round.
examples.zh: 老师把「严厉触发策略」与只持续一个课堂轮次的应对方式作了比较。

collocations: compare a grim trigger strategy with a temporary response

words.enDefinition: A repeated-game strategy that starts with cooperation and then copies the other player's previous action.

examples.en: The tit-for-tat strategy began with a contribution and then copied the other team's last move.
examples.zh: 「一报还一报策略」先从出资开始，之后照做另一队上一轮的行动。

examples.en: We discussed how a mistaken choice could affect both groups using the tit-for-tat strategy.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了，一次错误选择可能怎样影响两个采用「一报还一报策略」的小组。

collocations: compare a tit-for-tat strategy with always cooperating

words.enDefinition: A payoff expressed in present terms by giving later rewards less weight than earlier rewards.

examples.en: We calculated a discounted payoff for the option that delivered most of its points later.
examples.zh: 我们为大部分积分较晚发放的选项计算了「折现收益」。

examples.en: The tutor compared an immediate payoff with the discounted payoff from waiting one more round.
examples.zh: 老师比较了立刻获得的收益与再等一轮所得的「折现收益」。

collocations: calculate total discounted payoff over several rounds

words.enDefinition: The influence of expected future interactions on a player's willingness to cooperate now.

examples.en: The tutor introduced the shadow of the future when the same teams expected to meet again.
examples.zh: 原来的队伍预计还会继续碰面时，老师介绍了「未来的影子」。

examples.en: We discussed whether the shadow of the future changed how the clubs shared the studio today.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「未来的影子」是否改变了各社团当天共用工作室的做法。

collocations: explain the shadow of the future
discuss the shadow of the future
a longer shadow of the future

words.enDefinition: In suitable dynamic games, the rule that checking single-decision deviations suffices to verify equilibrium at every subgame.

examples.en: We applied the one-shot deviation principle by changing one action and keeping the remaining strategy fixed.
examples.zh: 我们应用「单次偏离原理」，改变一次行动，同时保持策略的其余部分不变。

examples.en: The worksheet tested the one-shot deviation principle at every decision in the small scheduling game.
examples.zh: 练习表在小型排期博弈的每个决策点检验了「单次偏离原理」。

collocations: use the one-shot deviation principle to verify an equilibrium
check the assumptions of the one-shot deviation principle

words.enDefinition: A result showing that many feasible individually rational payoffs can be sustained in repeated games under suitable conditions.

examples.en: Our tutor used a folk theorem to explain why patient players could sustain several different outcomes.
examples.zh: 老师用一条「民间定理」解释重视未来的参与者为何能维持几种不同结果。

examples.en: The worksheet asked which assumptions were needed before applying the folk theorem to the classroom game.
examples.zh: 练习表问，对课堂博弈使用「民间定理」之前需要哪些假设。

collocations: explain a folk theorem for repeated games
discuss the conditions of a folk theorem

words.enDefinition: A model of how players make offers or choose actions to reach an agreement.

examples.en: The bargaining game asked two clubs to agree on how to divide time in the shared studio.
examples.zh: 「讨价还价博弈」让两个社团商定怎样分配共用工作室的时间。

examples.en: Our tutor changed the order of offers in the bargaining game and compared the resulting choices.
examples.zh: 老师改变「讨价还价博弈」里提议的顺序，并比较由此产生的选择。

collocations: compare outcomes in a bargaining game

words.enDefinition: A game where one player proposes a division and the other either accepts or triggers disagreement payoffs for both.

examples.en: The ultimatum game asked one student to offer a division of ten classroom tokens to another.
examples.zh: 「最后通牒博弈」要求一名学生向另一名学生提议如何分配十枚课堂代币。

examples.en: We compared how often different offers were accepted in the classroom version of the ultimatum game.
examples.zh: 我们比较了课堂版「最后通牒博弈」中不同提议被接受的频率。

collocations: analyse offers in an ultimatum game
compare outcomes in an ultimatum game

words.enDefinition: An allocation game in which one player chooses the division and the recipient cannot reject it.

examples.en: The dictator game let one student divide ten tokens without asking the other student to approve.
examples.zh: 「独裁者博弈」允许一名学生分配十枚代币，无需征得另一名学生同意。

examples.en: Our tutor compared the dictator game with a version in which the second player could reject.
examples.zh: 老师把「独裁者博弈」与第二位参与者可以拒绝提议的版本作了比较。

collocations: compare allocations in a dictator game
contrast a dictator game with an ultimatum game

words.enDefinition: A bargaining procedure in which players take turns making offers until there is agreement or the game ends.

examples.en: The exercise used alternating-offers bargaining so each club could suggest a different division in turn.
examples.zh: 练习采用「交替出价谈判」，让各社团轮流提出不同的分配方案。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how a delay would change the proposals in the alternating-offers bargaining model.
examples.zh: 老师问，延迟将怎样改变「交替出价谈判」模型里的提议。

words.zhGloss: 只能接受或拒绝的提议
words.enDefinition: An offer the recipient can accept or reject without proposing a counteroffer within the game.
acceptedZhAnswers: 只能接受或拒绝的提议

examples.en: The worksheet gave the second club a take-it-or-leave-it offer for one hour of studio time.
examples.zh: 练习表给第二个社团一项「只能接受或拒绝的提议」，内容是一小时的工作室使用时间。

examples.en: The tutor asked when the responder would accept a take-it-or-leave-it offer in the classroom example.
examples.zh: 老师问，课堂例题中的回应者在什么情况下会接受这项「只能接受或拒绝的提议」。

words.enDefinition: The vector of payoffs the players receive if they fail to reach a bargain.

examples.en: We used the disagreement point to show what both clubs would receive without a shared booking.
examples.zh: 我们用「谈判破裂点」说明未达成共同预订时两个社团各能得到什么。

examples.en: Our tutor changed the disagreement point before recalculating how the shared time would be divided.
examples.zh: 老师先改变「谈判破裂点」，再重新计算共享时间会怎样分配。

collocations: compare offers with the disagreement point
set the disagreement point in a bargaining model

words.enDefinition: An alternative available to a participant outside the agreement being negotiated.

examples.en: One club had an outside option because another room was available for its workshop.
examples.zh: 因为还有另一间教室可用于举办工作坊，一个社团拥有「谈判外选择」。

examples.en: The tutor added an outside option to see whether the first club would accept fewer shared hours.
examples.zh: 老师加入一个「谈判外选择」，看看第一个社团是否会接受更少的共享时数。

collocations: compare an offer with an outside option
include an outside option in the game

words.enDefinition: The combined gains available from reaching an agreement relative to the disagreement outcome.

examples.en: The bargaining surplus came from both clubs gaining extra usable hours by sharing the studio.
examples.zh: 「谈判剩余」来自两个社团通过共用工作室获得更多可用时数。

examples.en: We calculated the bargaining surplus after comparing a shared booking with each club's fallback result.
examples.zh: 我们把共同预订与各社团谈不成时的结果作比较，计算了「谈判剩余」。

collocations: compare the bargaining surplus across agreements

words.enDefinition: in the two-player symmetric model, the feasible individually rational outcome maximising the product of both players' gains over disagreement

examples.en: The tutor used the Nash bargaining solution to divide the gains from a joint studio booking.
examples.zh: 老师用「纳什谈判解」分配共同预订工作室所获得的收益。

examples.en: We recalculated the Nash bargaining solution after one club gained access to another room.
examples.zh: 一个社团获准使用另一间教室后，我们重新计算了「纳什谈判解」。

collocations: compare a Nash bargaining solution across disagreement points

words.enDefinition: A parameter determining the relative weight given to a player's payoff gain in a bargaining solution.

examples.en: A larger bargaining weight increased the first club's share in the simplified model on our worksheet.
examples.zh: 练习表的简化模型中，更大的「谈判权重」提高了第一个社团的份额。

examples.en: The tutor varied one bargaining weight while leaving the disagreement payoffs unchanged in the example.
examples.zh: 老师调整了例题中的一个「谈判权重」，而谈不成时的收益保持原样。

words.enDefinition: A bargaining problem where dependence after a specific sunk investment weakens the investing party's position.

examples.en: The case illustrated a hold-up problem after one group built equipment suitable for only one shared venue.
examples.zh: 一个小组建造了只能用于某个共享场地的设备后，案例展示了由此出现的「套牢问题」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how an earlier agreement would affect the hold-up problem in the example.
examples.zh: 老师问，较早达成协议会怎样影响例题中的「套牢问题」。

collocations: discuss how a contract addresses a hold-up problem

words.enDefinition: An experiment or model where individuals choose contributions to a fund or activity that benefits the group.

examples.en: In the public goods game, each classroom token contributed to the fund benefited both teams.
examples.zh: 在「公共物品博弈」中，投入基金的每枚课堂代币都惠及两队。

examples.en: We compared contributions in the public goods game before and after participants saw the earlier group totals.
examples.zh: 我们比较了参与者看到此前各组合计前后，在「公共物品博弈」中的出资。

collocations: measure contributions in a public goods game

words.enDefinition: An experiment where one player sends an amount that may grow and the recipient chooses how much to return.

examples.en: The trust game gave the second student a choice about returning some of the classroom tokens.
examples.zh: 「信任博弈」让第二名学生决定是否归还部分课堂代币。

examples.en: We recorded the initial transfers and the amounts returned in each round of the trust game.
examples.zh: 我们记录了「信任博弈」每轮最初转交的数量和归还的数量。

collocations: record transfers in a trust game
compare return amounts in a trust game

words.enDefinition: A game where players decide how much to take from a shared resource that can be depleted.

examples.en: The class used a common-pool resource game to model how withdrawals reduced the shared stock of tokens.
examples.zh: 全班用「公共池资源博弈」模拟领取代币如何减少共享库存。

examples.en: We recorded choices in the common-pool resource game before comparing the amounts left in the pool.
examples.zh: 我们先记录「公共池资源博弈」中的选择，再比较池中剩余的数量。

collocations: record withdrawals in a common-pool resource game
compare rules in a common-pool resource game

words.enDefinition: A specific condition assigned to participants so its effect can be compared with other conditions.

examples.en: One experimental treatment showed previous contributions before participants made their next choice in the game.
examples.zh: 一种「实验处理条件」在参与者作出下一次博弈选择前展示此前的出资。

examples.en: Our tutor described the experimental treatment that changed the matching rule between rounds of the exercise.
examples.zh: 老师介绍了在练习各轮之间改变配对规则的「实验处理条件」。

words.enDefinition: A baseline experimental condition used to compare outcomes with a changed condition.

examples.en: The control treatment kept the original rules while the other group could see earlier contributions.
examples.zh: 「实验对照条件」沿用原规则，另一组则可以看到此前的出资。

examples.en: We compared choices in the control treatment with choices after the information display was introduced.
examples.zh: 我们把「实验对照条件」中的选择与引入信息显示后的选择作了比较。

collocations: compare outcomes with a control treatment
define the rules for the control treatment

words.enDefinition: Valuations assigned through an experiment's payoff rules so participants face known incentives in the model.

examples.en: The tutor assigned induced values by specifying how many points each item was worth to its holder.
examples.zh: 老师通过规定各物品对持有者值多少分，分配了「诱导价值」。

examples.en: We used induced values to know what each participant stood to gain in the practice auction.
examples.zh: 我们用「诱导价值」了解各参与者在练习拍卖中可能获得多少收益。

collocations: use induced values in an experiment
compare choices under different induced values

words.enDefinition: The points or other rewards a participant earns under the rules of an experiment.

examples.en: We calculated the experimental payoff from the tokens still held by each participant at the end.
examples.zh: 我们根据结束时各参与者仍持有的代币，计算了「实验收益」。

examples.en: The worksheet explained how the experimental payoff changed when the shared fund returned additional points.
examples.zh: 练习表解释了共享基金返还额外积分时，「实验收益」会怎样改变。

collocations: record the experimental payoff for each participant

words.enDefinition: An experimental method eliciting choices for several possible situations before participants learn which situation occurs.

examples.en: Using the strategy method, we asked each participant how they would respond to every possible offer.
examples.zh: 使用「策略法」时，我们询问各参与者会怎样回应每种可能的提议。

examples.en: The tutor used the strategy method to collect choices for situations that did not actually occur.
examples.zh: 老师用「策略法」收集了参与者对于未实际发生情形的选择。

collocations: compare the strategy method with direct responses
collect choices using the strategy method

words.enDefinition: A procedure asking participants to report their expectations or probabilities about outcomes or others' actions.

examples.en: The experiment used belief elicitation to ask people how likely they thought the other group would contribute.
examples.zh: 实验通过「信念测量」询问参与者认为另一组有多大可能出资。

examples.en: We recorded belief elicitation answers before showing participants how their partners had actually played.
examples.zh: 我们先记录「信念测量」的答案，再向参与者展示搭档实际怎样行动。

words.enDefinition: Assigning participants to interact without revealing their partners' identities.

examples.en: The experiment used anonymous matching so participants could not identify who made the other choice.
examples.zh: 实验采用「匿名配对」，让参与者无法识别另一项选择是谁作出的。

examples.en: We discussed how anonymous matching might affect behaviour in the repeated contribution exercise.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「匿名配对」可能怎样影响重复出资练习中的行为。

collocations: compare anonymous matching with known pairings

words.enDefinition: An auction in which bidders submit offers without seeing other bids before the bidding deadline.

examples.en: In the sealed-bid auction, students wrote their offers before looking at anyone else's card.
examples.zh: 在「密封出价拍卖」中，学生先写下报价，之后才能看其他人的卡片。

examples.en: The tutor used a sealed-bid auction to compare two different rules for determining payment.
examples.zh: 老师用「密封出价拍卖」比较两种确定付款金额的规则。

collocations: submit an offer in a sealed-bid auction
compare bids in a sealed-bid auction

words.enDefinition: a single-item auction in which the highest bidder wins and pays that bidder's own bid

examples.en: The winner of the first-price auction paid the number of tokens written on their own card.
examples.zh: 「第一价格拍卖」的赢者按自己卡片上写的数量支付代币。

examples.en: Our tutor checked whether the predicted prices changed when the worksheet switched to a first-price auction.
examples.zh: 练习表切换到「第一价格拍卖」后，老师核查了预测价格是否改变。

collocations: compare a first-price auction with a second-price auction
record payments in a first-price auction

words.enDefinition: a single-item auction in which the highest bidder wins and pays the second-highest bid

examples.en: The second-price auction awarded the book to the highest bidder but charged the second-highest offer.
examples.zh: 「第二价格拍卖」把书给出价最高者，但按第二高的报价收费。

examples.en: The tutor used a second-price auction to show why the winning bid need not equal the payment.
examples.zh: 老师用「第二价格拍卖」说明为什么获胜报价不一定等于付款金额。

collocations: record payment in a second-price auction
compare a second-price auction with a first-price one

words.enDefinition: An open auction in which bids rise until the highest remaining bidder wins.

examples.en: The classroom English auction began with a low price and ended when only one bidder remained.
examples.zh: 课堂的「英式拍卖」从低价开始，只剩一名竞价者时结束。

examples.en: We compared an English auction with a demonstration where offers were written privately on cards.
examples.zh: 我们把「英式拍卖」与将报价私下写在卡片上的演示作了比较。

collocations: model an English auction as ascending bids

words.enDefinition: An auction starting at a high announced price that falls until someone accepts it.

examples.en: In the Dutch auction, the displayed price fell until one participant accepted it for the sample book.
examples.zh: 在「荷兰式拍卖」中，显示价格不断下降，直到一位参与者接受该价格购买示例图书。

examples.en: We drew the price sequence for the Dutch auction before comparing it with the rising-price format.
examples.zh: 和价格上升的形式比较之前，我们先画出了「荷兰式拍卖」的价格序列。

collocations: accept the current price in a Dutch auction

words.enDefinition: The value a bidder assigns to the item, which can differ from the amount they bid.

examples.en: The worksheet listed each bidder valuation separately from the amount written on the corresponding offer card.
examples.zh: 练习表将各「竞价者估值」和对应报价卡上写的数额分开列出。

examples.en: Our tutor asked why a bidder valuation mattered when calculating the winner's payoff in the game.
examples.zh: 老师问，计算博弈获胜者的收益时，为什么要考虑「竞价者估值」。

collocations: observe a bidder valuation in an experiment
compare a bid with the bidder valuation

words.enDefinition: An auction in which each bidder knows their own value and learning others' valuations does not change it.

examples.en: The classroom private-value auction gave each participant a known personal value for the same sample book.
examples.zh: 课堂「私有价值拍卖」给每位参与者设定了自己已知的示例图书估值。

examples.en: Our tutor asked which assumptions made the game a private-value auction in the classroom exercise.
examples.zh: 老师问，在课堂练习中，哪些假设使这场博弈属于「私有价值拍卖」。

collocations: compare a private-value auction with a common-value auction

words.enDefinition: Known individual valuations that are statistically independent across bidders in an auction model.

examples.en: The classroom model assumed independent private values and gave each participant a separate randomly chosen number.
examples.zh: 课堂模型假定「独立私有价值」，给每位参与者分别指定一个随机数。

examples.en: We asked how the exercise would change if the assumption of independent private values no longer held.
examples.zh: 我们问，如果「独立私有价值」的假设不再成立，练习结果会怎样变化。

collocations: compare auctions under independent private values

words.enDefinition: An auction where the item's underlying value is the same for everyone but may be uncertain beforehand.

examples.en: The common-value auction offered a jar of tokens whose actual contents were unknown to the bidders.
examples.zh: 「共同价值拍卖」提供了一罐代币，但竞价者不知道罐里实际有多少枚。

examples.en: Our tutor explained why estimates could differ in a common-value auction even though the underlying value was shared.
examples.zh: 老师解释了为什么尽管标的实际价值对所有人相同，「共同价值拍卖」中的估计仍可能不同。

collocations: compare a common-value auction with a private-value auction
estimate value in a common-value auction

words.enDefinition: The tendency of a winning estimate in a common-value auction to overstate value, potentially causing overpayment.

examples.en: The exercise illustrated the winner's curse when the winning estimate exceeded the actual number of tokens.
examples.zh: 获胜估计值超过代币的实际数量时，练习展示了「赢者诅咒」。

examples.en: Our tutor discussed why a high initial estimate was associated with the winner's curse in the classroom simulation.
examples.zh: 老师讨论了为什么课堂模拟中的高初始估计值与「赢者诅咒」有关。

collocations: identify evidence of the winner's curse

words.enDefinition: Submitting a bid below one's own valuation in an auction model.

examples.en: The classroom records showed bid shading when offers were lower than the values assigned to those bidders.
examples.zh: 当报价低于分给对应竞价者的估值时，课堂记录显示了「压低报价」。

examples.en: The tutor asked how bid shading might change the chance of winning the classroom item.
examples.zh: 老师问，「压低报价」可能怎样改变赢得课堂标的物的机会。

collocations: explain bid shading in a first-price model

words.enDefinition: Submitting a bid equal to one's valuation in a model where values are defined for bidders.

examples.en: The worksheet illustrated truthful bidding by matching the number on each offer card to its assigned value.
examples.zh: 练习表把各报价卡上的数字与分配的估值对应起来，说明什么是「如实报价」。

examples.en: Our tutor discussed truthful bidding under the private-value assumptions of the second-price auction exercise.
examples.zh: 老师在第二价格拍卖练习的私有价值假设下讨论了「如实报价」。

collocations: compare bids with valuations to detect truthful bidding

words.enDefinition: Under standard independent private-value assumptions with risk-neutral bidders, formats with the same allocation rule and lowest-type payoff yield equal expected revenue.

examples.en: The revenue equivalence theorem linked two auction formats under the assumptions written on our worksheet.
examples.zh: 按照练习表所列的假设，「收益等价定理」将两种拍卖形式联系起来。

examples.en: Our tutor asked why risk neutrality mattered for the revenue equivalence theorem in the simple example.
examples.zh: 老师问，在这个简单例题中，风险中性为什么对「收益等价定理」重要。

collocations: check the assumptions of the revenue equivalence theorem
